D. Limitations and Generalisation Boundaries

Three important generalisation boundaries constrain the
reported results. First, the AI-generated class is represented
exclusively by Midjourney v5 outputs. While this produces a
classifier with strong discrimination of that generator’s spectral
signatures, the system’s performance on images from DALL-E 3,
Stable Diffusion XL, Adobe Firefly, and Imagen has not been
formally evaluated. Preliminary qualitative testing on 40 out-of-
distribution samples suggests accuracy degradation of 3–8
percentage points on images from generators with different
training data and noise schedules.
Second, the evaluation is limited to static images in JPEG and
PNG formats. The hybrid architecture has not been adapted to
video frames, where temporal consistency between adjacent
frames provides an additional discriminative signal that could
both improve accuracy and introduce new artefact classes not
present in still images. Third, the robustness evaluation at JPEG
Q=10 (81.0% accuracy) reveals a meaningful failure mode:
aggressive lossy compression, as commonly applied by
messaging platforms, degrades FFT features to the point where
the frequency branch contributes noise rather than signal, and the
model becomes effectively a two-branch CNN+ViT classifier
with correspondingly lower accuracy. Quantisation-aware
training of the FFT branch is a promising mitigation direction.

D. Limitations and Generalisation Boundaries

Three important generalisation boundaries constrain the
reported results. First, the AI-generated class is represented
exclusively by Midjourney v5 outputs. While this produces a
classifier with strong discrimination of that generator’s spectral
signatures, the system’s performance on images from DALL-E 3,
Stable Diffusion XL, Adobe Firefly, and Imagen has not been
formally evaluated. Preliminary qualitative testing on 40 out-of-
distribution samples suggests accuracy degradation of 3–8
percentage points on images from generators with different
training data and noise schedules.
Second, the evaluation is limited to static images in JPEG and
PNG formats. The hybrid architecture has not been adapted to
video frames, where temporal consistency between adjacent
frames provides an additional discriminative signal that could
both improve accuracy and introduce new artefact classes not
present in still images. Third, the robustness evaluation at JPEG
Q=10 (81.0% accuracy) reveals a meaningful failure mode:
aggressive lossy compression, as commonly applied by
messaging platforms, degrades FFT features to the point where
the frequency branch contributes noise rather than signal, and the
model becomes effectively a two-branch CNN+ViT classifier
with correspondingly lower accuracy. Quantisation-aware
training of the FFT branch is a promising mitigation direction.

D. Limitations and Generalisation Boundaries

Three important generalisation boundaries constrain the
reported results. First, the AI-generated class is represented
exclusively by Midjourney v5 outputs. While this produces a
classifier with strong discrimination of that generator’s spectral
signatures, the system’s performance on images from DALL-E 3,
Stable Diffusion XL, Adobe Firefly, and Imagen has not been
formally evaluated. Preliminary qualitative testing on 40 out-of-
distribution samples suggests accuracy degradation of 3–8
percentage points on images from generators with different
training data and noise schedules.
Second, the evaluation is limited to static images in JPEG and
PNG formats. The hybrid architecture has not been adapted to
video frames, where temporal consistency between adjacent
frames provides an additional discriminative signal that could
both improve accuracy and introduce new artefact classes not
present in still images. Third, the robustness evaluation at JPEG
Q=10 (81.0% accuracy) reveals a meaningful failure mode:
aggressive lossy compression, as commonly applied by
messaging platforms, degrades FFT features to the point where
the frequency branch contributes noise rather than signal, and the
model becomes effectively a two-branch CNN+ViT classifier
with correspondingly lower accuracy. Quantisation-aware
training of the FFT branch is a promising mitigation direction.
